newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan September index of leading indicators up.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan September index of leading indicators up.

text.p: Taiwan's index of leading business indicators, which forecasts peaks and troughs in the business cycle, rose in September from August, the cabinet's Council for Economic Planning and Development said on Monday.
The index gained 1.2 percentage points to 99.1 in September from August and the index of coincident indicators also rose, advancing 1.1 percentage point to 101.2 from a month ago.
The council said the economy turned to a "green light" condition from a "yellow blue light" in September.
It was the first "green light" condition since August 1995, indicating a possible recovery, the council noted.

Eighteen percent of a sample polling of manufacturing executives said the economy would turn worse, unchanged from in August, while 23 percent said the economy would improve, slightly down from 24 percent a month earlier.
Those who were optimistic about the economy outnumbered those who were pessimistic for a second straight month, the council said.
The remainder said the economy would remain unchanged.
Many analysts expect Taiwan's economy to gradually recover in the fourth quarter of 1996, spurred by improving export orders and industrial output.
